extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians / computational algebraists) using the spcurve, spectrum, surfacesignature and finvar libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (usage, assumptions, return values, notes and examples) for singularity and invariant-theory computations. Targeted at users invoking these library routines and interpreting their outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: relweight
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: relweight(N,W,a); N matrix, W intmat, a intvec. Assume: N is a non-zero matrix; W is an integer matrix of the same size as N; a is an integer vector giving the weights of the variables. Return: integer, max(a-weighted order(Nij) - Wij | all entries ij); string "ERROR" if sizes do not match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided showing loading spcurve.lib, defining ring, matrix N, intmat W and intvec a; returns 2 in the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: posweight
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: posweight(M,t1,n[,s]); M matrix, t1 module, n int, s string. n=0 : all deformations of non-negative weight; n=1 : only non-constant deformations of non-negative weight; n=2 : all deformations of positive weight. Assume: M is a presentation matrix of a Cohen-Macaulay codimension 2 ideal and t1 is its T1 space in matrix notation. Return: new ring containing a list posw, consisting of a presentation matrix describing the deformation given by the generators of T1 of non-negative/positive weight and the weight vector for the new variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The current basering should not contain any variables named T(i). Example shows using isCMcod2, matrixT1 and posweight, and printing posw results (presentation matrix and weight vector).

rubrics_metrics.name: KSpencerKernel
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: KSpencerKernel(M[,s][,v]); M matrix, s string, v intvec. Assume: M is a quasihomogeneous n x (n+1) matrix where the n minors define an isolated space curve singularity. Return: new ring containing the coefficient matrix KS representing the kernel of the Kodaira-Spencer map of the family of non-negative deformations having the given singularity as special fibre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: - initial basering should not contain variables named e(i) or T(i) (they are used internally). - setting an intvec watchProgress with 5 entries shows progress: watchProgress[1] -> option(prot) in groebner commands; [2] -> trace output for highcorner; [3] -> output of deformed matrix; [4] -> result of elimination step (and >1 -> additional trace); [5] -> matrix representing the kernel using print. Example demonstrates calling KSpencerKernel and printing KS, along with printed names and weights blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: spectrumnd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spectrumnd(f[,1]); poly f. Assume: basering has characteristic 0 and local ordering, f has isolated singularity at 0 and nondegenerate principal part. Return: list S: ideal S[1]: spectral numbers in increasing order; intvec S[2]: Int S[2][i]: multiplicity of spectral number S[1][i]. If a second argument 1 is given, no test for a degenerate principal part will be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEE ALSO: gmssing lib. Example shows computing spectrumnd on a specific polynomial and inspecting size and entries of the returned lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: signatureBrieskorn
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: signatureBrieskorn(a1,a2,a3); a1,a2,a3 = integers. Return: signature of Brieskorn singularity x^a1 + y^a2 + z^a3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: signatureBrieskorn(11,3,5) returns -48.

rubrics_metrics.name: signaturePuiseux
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: signaturePuiseux(N,f); N = int, f = irreducible poly in 2 variables. Return: signature of surface singularity defined by z^N + f(x,y) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates calling signaturePuiseux with a specific polynomial and integer N returning -92.

rubrics_metrics.name: signatureNemethi
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: signatureNemethi(N,f); N = integer, f = reduced poly in 2 variables, # empty or 1,2,3 - if #[1] = 1 then resolution of singularity is used - if #[1] = 2 then spectral pairs are used - if # is empty then both upper variants are used in parallel and the fastest returns the result. Return: signature of surface singularity defined by z^N + f(x,y) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: computes the signature of some special surface singularities. Example shows calling signatureNemethi with option 1 to force resolution, and printlevel to show messages (e.g., 'Resolution of singularity has been used.').

rubrics_metrics.name: invariant_ring
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariant_ring(G1,G2,...[,flags]); G1,G2,...: <matrices> generating a finite matrix group, flags: an optional <intvec> with three entries: if the first one equals 0, the program attempts to compute the Molien series and Reynolds operator, if it equals 1, the program is told that the Molien series should not be computed, if it equals -1 characteristic 0 is simulated (user must choose a field of large prime characteristic, e.g. 32003) and if the first one is anything else, it means that the characteristic of the base field divides the group order; the second component should give the size of intervals between canceling common factors in the expansion of Molien series; the third component controls display. Return: primary and secondary invariants for any matrix representation of a finite group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: information about stages if the third flag != 0. Theory: Bases of homogeneous invariants are generated successively and primary invariants are chosen to lower the dimension of the ideal generated by previously found invariants. Non-modular vs modular case handled differently (Reynolds operator and Molien series used in non-modular case; modular case follows Kemper 1996). Example shows returned primary and secondary invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariant_ring_random
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariant_ring_random(G1,G2,...,r[,flags]); G1,G2,... generating a finite matrix group, r: int range for coefficients of random combinations of basis elements that serve as primary invariants, flags as in invariant_ring. Return: primary and secondary invariants for any matrix representation of a finite group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same as invariant_ring except random combinations of basis elements are chosen as primary invariant candidates. Example shows usage and returned invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary_invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_invariants(G1,G2,...[,flags]); G1,G2,... generating a finite matrix group, flags: optional intvec with three entries (meanings as in invariant_ring). Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring and, if computable, Reynolds operator and Molien series or ring name (in char p case); if first flag is 1 and non-modular, an intvec of degrees with no non-trivial invariants may be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: info if third flag != 0. Theory: Bases of homogeneous invariants generated successively and chosen as primaries that lower the dimension. Example shows returned primary invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary_invariants_random
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_invariants_random(G1,G2,...,r[,flags]); same parameters as primary_invariants but random linear combinations are chosen as primary invariants candidates. Return: primary invariants and possibly Reynolds operator and Molien series or degree info (if first flag 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned primaries when randomization parameter r is provided. Same generation strategy as primary_invariants but candidates randomized.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariant_algebra_reynolds
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariant_algebra_reynolds(REY[,v]); REY: a g x n <matrix> representing the Reynolds operator of a finite matrix group (g = group order, n = number of variables of basering); v: optional int. Assume: non-modular case (characteristic of basering does not divide group order). Return: A minimal homogeneous generating set of the invariant ring (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: progress information if v != 0. Theory: incremental search in increasing degree; generators found among Reynolds images of monomials of degree d; chosen by Groebner basis techniques. Note: should not be used in rings with weighted orders. Example shows progress messages and returned generating set.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariant_algebra_perm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariant_algebra_perm(GEN[,v]); GEN: list of generators of a permutation group in disjoint cycle form (trivial cycles omitted). v: optional int. Assume: non-modular case (characteristic does not divide group order) — function does not verify this. Return: A minimal homogeneous generating set of the invariant ring of the group presented by GEN (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: progress information if v != 0. Theory: incremental search in degree d; generators found among orbit sums and selected by Groebner basis techniques. Note: should not be used in rings with weighted orders. Example demonstrates progress messages and returned generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: cyclotomic
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cyclotomic(i); i integer > 0. Returns: the i-th cyclotomic polynomial (type <poly>) as one in the first ring variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: x^i - 1 is divided by the j-th cyclotomic polynomial where j runs over proper divisors of i. Example: cyclotomic(25) -> x^20 + x^15 + x^10 + x^5 + 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: group_reynolds
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: group_reynolds(G1,G2,...[,v]); G1,G2,...: n x n matrices generating a finite matrix group, v: optional int. Assume: n is number of variables of basering, g is number of group elements. Return: a list whose first element will be a g x n matrix representing the Reynolds operator in the non-modular case; in characteristic >0 special additional information (lcm) may be returned; other list elements are the n x n matrices listing all group elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: information if v != 0. Theory: generates entire matrix group by left products, stores ring mappings as rows of the Reynolds matrix. Example shows returned mappings and matrix elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: molien(G1,G2,...[,ringname,lcm,flags]); G1,G2,...: n x n matrices (all elements of a finite matrix group), ringname: string for new ring of characteristic 0 for Molien series in prime characteristic case, lcm: int giving lcm of elements' orders (in prime characteristic), flags: optional intvec with three components (first non-zero simulates characteristic 0, second gives size of intervals between canceling common factors). Assume: n is number of variables of basering, G1,G2... are group elements generated by group_reynolds(), lcm is second return value of group_reynolds(). Return: in characteristic 0 a 1x2 matrix giving enumerator and denominator of Molien series; in prime characteristic a ring named 'ringname' of characteristic 0 is created where the Molien series (named M) is stored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: info if third component of flags != 0. Theory: in char 0 compute terms 1/det(1 - xE) for all group elements; in prime characteristic a Brauer lift is involved. Returned matrix gives enumerator and denominator of the expanded Molien series (common factors canceled). Examples illustrate both char 0 and prime char usage and creating/using the created ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: reynolds_molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: reynolds_molien(G1,G2,...[,ringname,flags]); G1,G2,...: n x n matrices generating a finite matrix group, ringname: optional string for new ring in prime characteristic case, flags: optional intvec. Assume: n is number of variables of basering, G1,G2... are group elements generated by group_reynolds(), g is the size of the group. Return: a g x n matrix representing the Reynolds operator as first return value and in char 0 a 1x2 matrix giving enumerator and denominator of Molien series as second; in prime characteristic a ring 'ringname' of characteristic 0 is created storing the Molien series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display information if third component of flags != 0. Theory: generates group elements and corresponding ring mappings; in char 0 computes 1/det(1-xE) terms as new elements found; in prime char uses Brauer lift and computes terms after full group generation. Example demonstrates usage and returned REY and M.

rubrics_metrics.name: partial_molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: partial_molien(M,n[,p]); M: a 1x2 matrix (Molien series), n: int number of terms in expansion, p: optional poly (previous intermediate result). Assume: M is return value of molien or second return value of reynolds_molien, p ought to be second return value of previous partial_molien and avoids recalculating known terms. Return: n terms (type <poly>) of the partial expansion of the Molien series (first n if no third parameter given, otherwise next n terms) and an intermediate result (type <poly>) for use in subsequent runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The calculation implements formal series division/expansion. Example shows successive calls to partial_molien and inspecting returned polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: evaluate_reynolds
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: evaluate_reynolds(REY,I); REY: a matrix representing the Reynolds operator, I: an ideal. Assume: REY is first return value of group_reynolds() or reynolds_molien(); the characteristic of the coefficient field should not divide the order of the finite matrix group. Returns: image of the polynomials defining I under the Reynolds operator (type <ideal>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: REY has been constructed so that each row serves as a ring mapping used by the Reynolds operator. Example shows mapping ideal x2,y2,z2 to their Reynolds images.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariant_basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariant_basis(g,G1,G2,...); g: int degree (>0) of homogeneous basis desired, G1,G2,... generating a finite matrix group. Returns: the basis (type <ideal>) of the space of invariants of degree g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: generate general polynomial of degree g, apply group generators, form linear system from differences equated to 0 and solve via syzygies. Example returns x2+y2 and z2 for degree 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariant_basis_reynolds
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariant_basis_reynolds(REY,d[,flags]); REY: matrix representing Reynolds operator, d: int degree (>0), flags: optional intvec with two entries: flags[1] gives the dimension of the space (default 0 meaning unknown) and flags[2] is used as the number of polynomials to map to invariants per call to evaluate_reynolds when dimension unknown (or such that number x dimension polynomials are mapped in one call when known). Assume: REY is first return value of group_reynolds() or reynolds_molien() and flags[1] given by partial_molien. Return: basis (type <ideal>) of space of invariants of degree d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Monomials of degree d are mapped to invariants via Reynolds operator; a linearly independent set is obtained using minbase. Example shows flags use and returned basis elements for degree 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary_char0
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_char0(REY,M[,v]); REY: matrix representing the Reynolds operator, M: 1x2 matrix representing the Molien series, v: optional int. Assume: REY is first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien and M the one of molien or second of reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: information about stages if v != 0. Theory: Bases of homogeneous invariants generated successively and chosen as primary invariants lowering the dimension of the ideal generated by previously found invariants. Example shows returned primaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary_charp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp(REY,ringname[,v]); REY: matrix representing the Reynolds operator, ringname: string giving the name of a ring where the Molien series is stored, v: optional int. Assume: REY is first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien and ringname names a characteristic 0 ring created by molien or reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: information about stages if v != 0. Theory and example analogous to primary_char0 but for prime characteristic workflow using the created ring storing Molien series.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary_char0_no_molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_char0_no_molien(REY[,v]); REY: matrix representing the Reynolds operator, v: optional int. Assume: REY is first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring and an intvec listing some degrees where no non-trivial homogeneous invariants are to be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: information about stages if v != 0. Theory: Bases of homogeneous invariants generated successively and chosen as primaries lowering dimension. Example shows returned primaries and degree info.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary_charp_no_molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp_no_molien(REY[,v]); REY: matrix representing the Reynolds operator, v: optional int. Assume: REY is first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring and an intvec listing some degrees where no non-trivial homogeneous invariants are to be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: info if v != 0. Example demonstrates usage in char p ring with returned primaries identical to char0 example.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary_charp_without
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp_without(G1,G2,...[,v]); G1,G2,...: matrices generating a finite matrix group, v: optional int. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: information about stages if v != 0. Example context is similar to other primary_* procedures; used when working directly in char p without prior Molien/Reynolds ring creation.
